figure_id.description: the figure's id: every turn runs in the audience `member:<figure_id>`; the last part of the phone's `chat_id`

world_id.description: the world's id: channels `world:<world_id>`, `phone:<world_id>`, `interview:<world_id>`; the middle part of the phone's `chat_id`

role.description: `human-sim` or `npc`: the frame the agent gets at boot (`instructions.role`); any other value refuses every turn with `role_unknown`

phone.description: `{enabled, speaker, contact}`: `enabled` offers `phone_message` on world turns (role `human-sim` only); `speaker` `member` (chat prefix `hp`) or `game_agent` (prefix `game`, hop `speaker`); `contact` names the sender of a phone turn. Given whole: a top-level key replaces the shipped object

extra_tools.description: client tools (provider schemas `{name, description, parameters}`) the figure offers on every turn beside the world's menu: a call of one leaves the figure on its rim as `calls` (hop `tool_name`), its `tool_result` comes back on the rim into the same turn. A name the turn already offers stays the world's; an extra call is no action in the world. Empty: the turns of before, byte for byte

description.purpose: Adapts the world's lanes to the agent's turn door: an obs, a phone message and an interview each become one turn, one at a time; the agent's client calls become world calls; a night becomes the close of every session of the day.
description.not_in_scope: No model call, no memory, no world knowledge, no deadline of its own.
description.emits_meaning: rim lanes with `hop.figure_rim` = out (an extra tool's `calls` among them); turns, tool results, closes and packs inward; `phone_out` to the handset.
description.consumes_meaning: the world's lanes, an extra tool's `tool_result` from the rim, the agent's answers, calls, errors, close reports and pack receipts, the handset's `phone_in`.
examples: obs -> turn; calls -> call; call_result -> tool_result; answer -> intent
